hcx.d: the shape is held bigger than it is, and the gap is defended
other people are read as terrain, and the move is made before it is felt
the structure gives way downward and stays down
nothing is allowed out of its cell, including you
the swing overshoots at both ends and never settles at the middle
the outline holds and there is nobody inside it

negotiator.h: You mean to start. In the pause before you begin, a reasonable voice speaks up. Just this once. You've earned a break. It never says stop for good, only stop for today. For a moment the easier option feels earned. Then the thing you meant to do is still waiting, and the next pause is easier to win. Reflection: What does the pause help you avoid feeling, and what would make beginning manageable?
negotiator.a: Everyone has a pause before starting. When the fear isn't the one talking in it, the gap between meaning to and beginning gets short. Trust becomes available that you can handle the first uncomfortable minute, and vitality goes into the thing itself.
negotiator.n: Notice the pause between meaning to and starting. Separate the reasonable voice from the discomfort it is steering you around. Choose the first small motion before the argument finishes.

micromanager.h: The future feels uncertain. Something may happen, but you cannot quite predict what. That uncertainty can produce anxiety before anything has actually gone wrong. The grip tightens in an attempt to make the outcome predictable: you check, correct, and take over. For a moment, control can feel like safety and the anxiety may ease. Then the room gets smaller: less space for the people around you to move, less room in you to trust without checking first. This is one possible pattern, not an explanation for every act of control. Reflection: When you cannot predict the outcome, what do you feel you need to take control of?
micromanager.a: Control isn't the problem. It works. When the fear isn't the one holding the grip, there's a beat of equanimity before you act, long enough to decide instead of react. Trust becomes available instead of something to verify first.
micromanager.n: Notice the moment the grip tightens. Separate the real risk from the old fear running it. Choose the next move from there.

victim.h: Something goes wrong and somebody asks what part was yours. The first answer that comes is the list of what was done to you. You tell it again. People lean in. For a moment the attention feels like being held. Then nothing has moved, and the next thing that goes wrong lands on the same spot. Reflection: What happened to you, and what part of the situation is still yours to influence?
victim.a: The hurt might be real. Some of it probably was done to you. When the charge isn't telling the story, there's room to find the one part that is yours to move. Equanimity becomes available to look at it without a fight, vitality to act on it, and joy has a way back in.
victim.n: Notice the moment the story starts to replay. Separate what happened to you from what is still in your hands. Choose one thing in your hands and do it.

perfectionist.h: The work is nearly done. You see one more flaw, then another, in your work and in other people's. You fix it. You hold it back a little longer. For a moment the extra pass feels like care. Then the deadline slides, the work never leaves your hands, and the people around you feel the pressure too. Reflection: Which flaw genuinely matters, and what are you asking the extra pass to protect you from?
perfectionist.a: High standards make good work. When the charge isn't setting them, there's room to see a finished thing as finished. Acceptance becomes available for work that has flaws, and equanimity when somebody else's work does too.
perfectionist.n: Notice the urge for one more pass. Separate the flaw that matters from the pressure to keep going. Choose a time to hand it over, and hand it over then.

pleaser.h: Somebody might be let down. A limit is needed, and the limit could cost their approval. So you help instead. You smooth it over, pay a compliment, take on the extra job. For a moment the room stays warm. Then your own preference has gone unsaid again, and the tiredness is the kind rest doesn't fix. Reflection: What do you actually want here, and what do you fear might happen if you say it plainly?
pleaser.a: Helping can be generous. When the fear isn't asking for approval, there's room to say what you want once and let it stand. Trust becomes available that the relationship can hold a no, and vitality comes back to what you choose to give.
pleaser.n: Notice the moment you reach to smooth things over. Separate what you want from what will keep them pleased. Choose to say the preference once, with no apology attached.

hyper achiever.h: Rest is available. Nobody is measuring anything. Something in you won't let the time sit empty. You open the laptop. You find one more thing to finish. For a moment the output feels like proof of your worth. Then the proof wears off by evening, and the next day needs more of it. Reflection: If your output did not prove anything about your worth, what would you choose to do next?
hyper achiever.a: Real work gets done this way. When the fear isn't keeping score, there's room for an hour that produces nothing. Vitality becomes available that doesn't come from output, and trust that your worth is still there when you stop.
hyper achiever.n: Notice the reach for the next task when rest is on offer. Separate what needs doing from what the output is meant to show. Choose an hour with nothing to show for it.

hyper rational.h: Somebody brings a feeling into the room. You go straight to the problem. You ask for the facts, find the logic, offer the fix. The feeling gets set aside as noise. For a moment the clarity feels like help. Then the other person goes quiet, and whatever you felt yourself never got named. Reflection: What feeling might need to be heard before you try to solve the problem?
hyper rational.a: Logic solves real things. When the charge isn't steering away from feeling, there's room to let an emotion count as information. Groundedness becomes available when a feeling shows up, and acceptance of what can't be explained yet.
hyper rational.n: Notice the jump from a feeling to a fix. Separate the problem from what the person in front of you feels. Choose to name the feeling first, then think.

hyper vigilant.h: Something in the room changes. Somebody asks you to trust them. Your attention goes to the exits, the risks, what could go wrong next. You scan. You plan around it. For a moment the watching feels like protection. Then the scan never switches off, and nothing gets to feel safe for long. Reflection: What is a real risk in front of you, and what is a possibility your attention keeps rehearsing?
hyper vigilant.a: Watching has kept you out of real trouble. When the fear isn't running the scan, there's room to notice what is safe right now. Trust becomes available in small amounts, and equanimity when the room changes again.
hyper vigilant.n: Notice the scan starting when something changes. Separate the real risk in front of you from the one that is always just ahead. Choose one thing that is safe and stay with it for a minute.

restless.h: Things settle. The job, the place, the plan starts to feel familiar. An itch starts. You look for the next thing, a new project, a new place, a new plan. For a moment the new thing feels alive. Then it settles too, and the itch comes back on schedule. Reflection: Are you moving toward something meaningful, or away from the discomfort of staying?
restless.a: Curiosity moves things forward. When the charge isn't pushing you out of the moment, there's room to stay long enough for something to deepen. Vitality becomes available in the familiar thing, and trust that staying won't trap you.
restless.n: Notice the itch when things go quiet and steady. Separate real curiosity from the push to leave. Choose to stay twice as long as the itch wants.

stickler.h: Somebody does it differently. The dishwasher is loaded wrong, the report is out of order, the plan skipped a step. You feel the wrongness before you think about it. You correct it. You explain the right way. For a moment the order feels like relief. Then people stop doing things around you, and you end up doing everything the right way alone. Reflection: Which standard matters here, and where could another workable approach be acceptable?
stickler.a: Order helps. When the charge isn't enforcing it, there's room to tell a standard you value from one that only keeps the fear down. Acceptance becomes available for another way that works, and equanimity when things are out of place.
stickler.n: Notice the jolt when something is done another way. Separate the standard you value from the fear it is guarding. Choose which one to act on.

judge.h: Somebody falls short, and sometimes that somebody is you. The verdict arrives fast. You find the fault. You replay the old failures that seem to back it up. For a moment the judgment feels like seeing clearly. Then the same eye turns on everything, and every other pattern has something to feed on. Reflection: What specifically went wrong, without turning it into a verdict about the person?
judge.a: Some things really are wrong. When the charge isn't passing the sentence, there's room to see what is also right about the same situation. Acceptance becomes available toward others and toward you, along with equanimity and the vitality the verdicts were using up.
judge.n: Notice the verdict as it forms. Separate what actually went wrong from who you're blaming for it. Choose to find one thing that is right about it.

deflector.h: Somebody asks a direct question, or something asks you to own your part. You change the subject. You explain why it wasn't really you. You make a joke. For a moment the attention moves somewhere safer. Then the question is still there, and the person asking learns less about you each time. Reflection: What part of the question feels hardest to answer directly?
deflector.a: Some things can stay private. When the shame isn't steering the answer, there's room to stay with the question long enough to answer it. Worth becomes available that doesn't depend on staying unseen, and equanimity when someone looks closely.
deflector.n: Notice the swerve when a direct question lands. Separate what is being asked from what you fear it shows. Choose to stay with the question for ten seconds before you answer.

dramatizer.h: A strong feeling arrives and people are around. The volume goes up. You tell it bigger. The story gets sharper with each telling. For a moment the room moves and the feeling is seen. Then people start bracing when you speak, and the real size of what you felt gets lost. Reflection: What is the feeling at its actual size, before the story around it grows?
dramatizer.a: The feeling may be big. When the charge isn't turning it up, there's room to say it at the size it actually is. Groundedness becomes available inside a strong feeling, and joy that doesn't need an audience.
dramatizer.n: Notice the volume rising as you start to speak. Separate the size of the feeling from the size of the telling. Choose to say the next part at half the volume.

worrywart.h: The future is unclear. Your mind runs ahead to what could go wrong. You picture it. You picture the next one. Then you go back and run the first one again. For a moment the worry feels like getting ready. Then nothing has been decided, and you're worn out by a day that hasn't happened. Reflection: What is one specific risk you can prepare for, and what remains uncertain rather than actionable?
worrywart.a: Plans need some thinking ahead. When the fear isn't running the forecast, there's room to name one real risk and one real answer to it. Trust becomes available in your ability to handle what comes, and joy in the day you're actually in.
worrywart.n: Notice the loop when a new worry starts. Separate the specific worst case from the general dread. Choose one action you would take if it happened, and stop there.

loner.h: Connection is on offer. Somebody invites you in, or help would make this easier. You decline. You handle it alone, and it feels like preferring your own company. For a moment the distance feels like strength. Then the gap gets wider, and asking gets harder the longer it goes. Reflection: Do you genuinely want solitude right now, or does needing someone feel too risky?
loner.a: Solitude can be good. When the fear isn't choosing it for you, there's room to want people and to let them in. Trust becomes available in the people close to you, and joy in being with them.
loner.n: Notice the step back when connection is offered. Separate wanting time alone from avoiding the risk of needing someone. Choose one direct ask for company or help.

people pleaser.h: You can't tell if they approve. A boundary would help, and it might cost their liking you. You adjust. You agree. You say what lands well over what's true. For a moment their warmth feels like being all right. Then you can't remember what you actually think, and the relationship is with someone you're performing. Reflection: What answer would be honest and considerate, even if it does not win approval?
people pleaser.a: Caring what people think keeps you connected. When the shame isn't asking for approval, there's room to give the answer that's good for the relationship. Worth becomes available that doesn't hang on their face, and vitality in being yourself with them.
people pleaser.n: Notice the shift as you read their reaction. Separate what serves the relationship from what wins their approval. Choose the first one.

skeptic.h: Something new arrives that doesn't fit what you already think. The doubt comes first. You look for the flaw. You find a reason it won't work. For a moment the doubt feels like protection from being fooled. Then nothing new gets in, and the picture you're holding stops matching the world. Reflection: What evidence would help you evaluate this fairly without dismissing it in advance?
skeptic.a: Good questions catch real mistakes. When the charge isn't guarding you against disappointment, there's room to let a new idea sit before you decide. Acceptance becomes available for what doesn't fit yet, and groundedness when it shakes something you believed.
skeptic.n: Notice the first reason to dismiss it. Separate a real flaw from the old guard against being let down. Choose to sit with it for a day before deciding.

dreamer.h: You can see how good it could be, and how far away it is. The gap shows, and you go back to the picture. You refine the vision. You wait for better conditions. For a moment the dream feels close. Then the gap stays the same size, and the dream gets harder to look at. Reflection: What is one small action that would bring the vision into contact with reality?
dreamer.a: Vision points somewhere worth going. When the charge isn't keeping you in the picture, there's room to take the first clumsy step. Vitality becomes available in the work itself, and joy in the thing as it actually gets built.
dreamer.n: Notice the drift back to the vision when the gap shows. Separate the picture from the next step it needs. Choose one concrete step and do it today.

procrastinator.h: The important thing is clear, and nothing stands in the way of starting. So you do something else. You tidy, plan, answer messages, stay busy. For a moment the motion feels like progress. Then the deadline gets close, the pressure arrives, and the work gets done in a rush you call your style. Reflection: What makes the first step difficult, and what is the smallest useful start?
procrastinator.a: Some things do need time. When the fear isn't pushing the start back, there's room to begin before you feel ready. Trust becomes available that a rough start is still a start, and joy in work that gets done without a panic.
procrastinator.n: Notice the side task you pick up in its place. Separate getting ready from actually beginning. Choose to begin for three minutes.

imposter.h: Somebody praises the work, or the work is about to be judged. A cold drop arrives. You wave the praise off. You over prepare. You wait to be found out. For a moment playing small feels safer. Then the evidence of what you can do keeps piling up, and none of it lands. Reflection: What evidence of your ability are you discounting, and what do you still need to learn?
imposter.a: Humility keeps you learning. When the shame isn't grading you, there's room to count what you actually know. Worth becomes available from the evidence that's already there, and trust that you earned your place in the room.
imposter.n: Notice the wave off as praise arrives. Separate what you know from what you fear they'll see. Choose one thing you know that the room doesn't, and say it.

aggressor.h: Somebody pushes back, or the plan stalls. The heat comes up fast. You raise your voice. You push harder. You override. For a moment it works, people fall in line. Then the agreement turns out to be fear, and what they actually think goes underground. Reflection: What is the real issue beneath the heat, and how could you address it without intimidation?
aggressor.a: Sometimes things need pushing. When the anger isn't the one pushing, there's room for a pause long enough to see what's underneath it. Equanimity becomes available when you're challenged, and vitality that doesn't need a fight.
aggressor.n: Notice the heat as somebody pushes back. Separate the anger from the fear underneath it. Choose your next words after a five second pause.

martyr.h: Giving can become a way to make yourself necessary. You say yes when you mean no. You carry what somebody else could carry. You wait for the sacrifice to be noticed, and when it isn't, something in you hardens. Reflection: Would you still choose to give this if nobody noticed or owed you anything?
martyr.a: The giving might be real. So might the exhaustion. What matters is whether it was freely chosen, or whether giving became the way a place got earned. When the charge isn't driving it, there's room to ask what you actually want to do. Worth becomes available instead of something to earn, with room for joy and vitality in what you choose to give.
martyr.n: Notice the give before you've offered it. Separate what you want to do from what you feel is owed. Choose from the first one.

cynic.h: Someone gets excited, or you catch yourself hoping. You get there first with the reason it won't last. You roll your eyes. You name the catch. For a moment being unimpressed feels safe from disappointment. Then the hope in the room dries up, including yours. Reflection: What is genuinely flawed here, and what might still be worthwhile?
cynic.a: Some things are overhyped. When the charge isn't dismissing it in advance, there's room to see what is actually good. Acceptance becomes available for hope that might not work out, and joy in it while it's here.
cynic.n: Notice the eye roll before you say it. Separate a real catch from the guard against being let down. Choose to name one good thing about it.

manipulator.h: You need something, and asking straight out feels too exposed. So you go around. You hint. You hold something back until they offer. You set things up so they come to you. For a moment it works, and you never had to ask. Then people sense the angle, and trust gets thinner each time. Reflection: What do you need, and what would it look like to ask for it directly?
manipulator.a: Everyone has needs. When the charge isn't steering around the ask, there's room to say the need straight. Equanimity becomes available for hearing yes or no, and the vitality that went into the setup comes back.
manipulator.n: Notice the angle forming before you ask. Separate the actual need from the setup around it. Choose to say the need once, directly.

overthinker.h: A decision is due and the outcome is unclear. You look at it again. You weigh one more angle. You ask one more person. For a moment the thinking feels responsible. Then the loop runs past anything new to learn, and the clock makes the choice for you. Reflection: What information is still missing, and when will more thinking stop helping?
overthinker.a: Some choices need thinking through. When the fear isn't asking for certainty, there's room to decide with what you know. Trust becomes available in a good enough choice, and worth that doesn't depend on getting it perfect.
overthinker.n: Notice the loop once you've stopped learning anything new. Separate the information you need from the certainty you want. Choose a time to decide, and decide then.

escapist.h: Something uncomfortable starts, and there's a way out. You reach for the phone, the snack, the drink, the drive. For a moment the feeling goes quiet. Then it comes back unfinished, and the exits get used more often. Reflection: Do you need a restorative break, or are you leaving before you can name what you feel?
escapist.a: A break can help. When the fear isn't reaching for the exit, there's room to stay with a hard feeling until it moves. Vitality becomes available in being here, and trust that you can get through discomfort without leaving.
escapist.n: Notice the reach for the exit. Separate needing a real break from leaving before the feeling finishes. Choose to stay for two minutes and name what's there.

avoider.h: Something needs dealing with, and leaving it costs nothing today. So it slides. You don't argue with it or run from it. You just don't look. For a moment nothing can land on you. Then the pile grows quietly, and the bill comes due all at once. Reflection: What is the real reason this can wait, or what makes it difficult to face now?
avoider.a: Some things can wait. When the fear isn't keeping your eyes off it, there's room to look at the thing directly. Vitality becomes available for the smallest piece of it, and trust that you can handle what you find.
avoider.n: Notice the thing you keep not looking at. Separate what can wait from what you're avoiding. Choose to say it out loud, then do the smallest piece.

nihilist.h: Effort needs a reason, and the reason starts to look thin. You knock it down before it can let you down. You call it pointless. You stop trying. For a moment nothing can disappoint you. Then nothing can reach you either, and the days go flat. Reflection: Even without a complete answer about meaning, what still matters enough to do?
nihilist.a: Big questions are worth asking. When the charge isn't answering them in advance, there's room to do something worth doing anyway. Acceptance becomes available for not having the full answer, and joy in what you do meanwhile.
nihilist.n: Notice the moment you call it pointless. Separate the honest question from the guard against disappointment. Choose one thing worth doing either way, and do it.

innocent.h: Things get complicated. A conflict starts, or a choice carries moral weight. You step back. You don't ask. You let yourself not know. For a moment staying out of it keeps you clean. Then something you could have seen happens anyway, and staying out made you part of it. Reflection: What do you already know about this situation that you have not wanted to acknowledge?
innocent.a: Not every fight is yours. When the fear isn't closing your eyes, there's room to see what you already know. Trust becomes available that you can face it, and that knowing won't sink you.
innocent.n: Notice the step back when it gets complicated. Separate what isn't yours from what you're pretending not to see. Choose to name one thing you already know.

pessimist.h: A good outcome becomes possible. You start building the case against it. You list what will go wrong. You lower your hopes before anyone else can. For a moment expecting the worst feels like protection. Then you put in less, the outcome gets smaller, and the case comes true. Reflection: What is the realistic risk, and what is the best plausible outcome worth acting toward?
pessimist.a: Some plans do fail. When the charge isn't writing the ending, there's room to picture the good outcome as clearly as the bad one. Trust becomes available that it might work, and joy in giving it a real try.
pessimist.n: Notice the case building against a good outcome. Separate the real risk from the guard against hope. Choose the best thing that could really happen, and act from there.

catastrophizer.h: Something is unresolved. A message goes unanswered, a result is pending. In seconds it stops being an unknown and becomes the end of everything. You feel the grief of it ahead of time. For a moment you feel braced. Then the body pays for a disaster that hasn't happened, and usually never does. Reflection: What do you know right now, and what part of the outcome are you imagining?
catastrophizer.a: Some things are serious. When the fear isn't jumping to the end, there's room to see where things actually stand right now. Trust becomes available in the facts in front of you, and joy in a day that isn't a disaster.
catastrophizer.n: Notice the jump from not knowing to the worst. Separate what is true right now from what you're picturing. Choose to describe the situation as it is, in the present tense.

enabler.h: Someone you care about is doing the harmful thing again. You see it. You don't say it. You cover for them, lend the money, make the excuse. For a moment the peace holds and they stay close. Then the pattern grows, and the silence is part of what keeps it going. Reflection: How can you care about this person without covering for behavior that is causing harm?
enabler.a: Standing by people matters. When the shame isn't keeping you quiet, there's room to say what you see once and let them answer. Worth becomes available that doesn't depend on them staying, and vitality that was going into covering for them.
enabler.n: Notice the moment you start to cover for them. Separate keeping the peace from keeping the pattern. Choose to say what you see, once, and let them answer.

control freak.h: You walk into something you didn't set up. A plan you didn't design. A silence where a yes should be. You start running it before any gap opens. You scan ahead for what could go wrong, and check that you're the one in charge. To other people it looks like competence. In the body it never lands, and the scan becomes the normal state. Reflection: What genuinely needs your attention, and what could safely remain in someone else's hands?
control freak.a: People rely on what you can do. When the fear isn't running the scan, there's room for your body to land in the room you're in. Presence becomes available here and not ahead, equanimity in a plan you didn't design, and trust in other people's hands.
control freak.n: Notice the jaw, the shoulders and the breath already locked. Separate the work in front of you from the scan running ahead of it. Choose to loosen them on the out breath, and see what still needs you.

grandiosity.behavior: May appear as superiority claims, status-seeking, special-rule expectations, dismissal of feedback, or using admiration to stabilize self-worth.
grandiosity.triggerMechanism: Possible triggers include perceived disrespect, criticism, loss of status, shame, or a threat to the preferred self-image. This is a working formulation, not a universal cause.
grandiosity.livedExample: After receiving corrective feedback, a person dismisses the source as inferior and insists ordinary standards do not apply to them.
grandiosity.impact: Can impair reciprocity, learning, trust, and accountability when the pattern dominates; assess observable behavior and context rather than assigning an identity.
grandiosity.practice: Describe the observable event without ranking people; identify the threatened need; invite disconfirming evidence; acknowledge one specific contribution or boundary from another person.
grandiosity.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart emphasizing stable self-respect without superiority: equal human worth, realistic appraisal, openness to feedback, and respect for others’ agency.

predatory.behavior: May include cold strategic pressure, exploitation, concealment of intent, treating people as obstacles, or planning actions without regard for harm.
predatory.triggerMechanism: May be activated by a perceived obstacle, rival, threat, or desired gain. This describes a possible pattern, not a diagnosis or a claim about any person.
predatory.livedExample: A person quietly plans how to remove a rival and evaluates only whether the plan will succeed, not the foreseeable harm.
predatory.impact: Can create significant relational or physical risk. Prioritize concrete behavior, boundaries, and safety; do not infer this mode from a label alone.
predatory.practice: Stop the harmful action; state the intended outcome and who could be affected; assess consent and foreseeable harm; choose a lawful, transparent alternative and seek appropriate support if safety is at risk.
predatory.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart that pursues legitimate goals transparently while respecting consent, safety, rights, and the other party’s independent interests.

collapse.behavior: May appear as shutdown, giving up, passivity, inability to initiate, or treating a difficult state as proof that no useful action is possible.
collapse.triggerMechanism: Possible triggers include overwhelm, repeated perceived failure, threat, exhaustion, or loss. The label is a working hypothesis and must not be used to infer a medical condition.
collapse.livedExample: After a setback, a person stops seeking options and concludes that no action can change the outcome.
collapse.impact: May narrow problem-solving and access to support. Similar outward behavior can have many causes, so assess context and needs rather than pathologizing it.
collapse.practice: Reduce the task to one safe, observable next step; identify available support; distinguish present constraints from global conclusions; seek professional care when distress is severe or persistent.
collapse.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart emphasizing grounded support, small feasible actions, restored choice, and realistic hope without denying pain or constraints.

rigidity.behavior: May appear as all-or-nothing standards, repeated insistence on one correct method, intolerance of ambiguity, or prioritizing control over adaptation.
rigidity.triggerMechanism: Possible triggers include uncertainty, perceived disorder, mistakes, or threat to predictability. These are hypotheses to test, not assumed causes.
rigidity.livedExample: A plan no longer fits the situation, but a person insists on following it because changing course feels unacceptable.
rigidity.impact: Can impair adaptation, collaboration, and repair; structure itself is not the problem unless it overrides evidence, context, or people’s needs.
rigidity.practice: Name the purpose behind the rule; list what has changed; generate two safe alternatives; retain the principle while adapting the method.
rigidity.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart that preserves values and accountability while adapting methods to evidence, context, and legitimate needs.

dysregulation.behavior: May include rapid escalation, abrupt shifts, impulsive action, or difficulty returning to baseline after activation; record the actual observed behavior.
dysregulation.triggerMechanism: Activation can be shaped by stress, unmet needs, threat, sleep, environment, and other factors. Do not assume a single cause or diagnosis.
dysregulation.livedExample: During conflict, activation rises quickly and the person acts before checking the facts or considering consequences.
dysregulation.impact: Can strain relationships and decision-making. This record is a descriptive aid, not a substitute for assessment of medical or mental-health concerns.
dysregulation.practice: Pause when safe; orient to immediate facts; reduce stimulation; use a practiced grounding or regulation skill; revisit the decision after activation decreases.
dysregulation.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart emphasizing awareness of activation, proportionate response, recovery, and deliberate choice without suppressing legitimate emotion.

dissociation.behavior: Possible signs can include feeling detached, emotionally distant, unreal, or disconnected from the present; these signs are nonspecific and should not be used to diagnose dissociation.
dissociation.triggerMechanism: Dissociative experiences can have multiple causes and require careful contextual assessment. Do not presume trauma, disorder, or a specific mechanism from this label.
dissociation.livedExample: In a stressful interaction, a person reports feeling distant from the situation and has difficulty staying connected to what is happening.
dissociation.impact: May affect presence, communication, and recall. If symptoms are recurrent, distressing, or impairing, recommend assessment by a qualified health professional.
dissociation.practice: Use a gentle present-orientation exercise if welcome and safe; invite the person to notice current surroundings and choices; avoid forcing recall or exposure; seek qualified support for persistent symptoms.
dissociation.inverseDefinition: An inferred counterpart emphasizing safe contact with present experience, continuity between feeling and action, and paced integration without forcing or denying experience.

painreg.common: tension headache, migraine, jaw clench, eye strain
painreg.pattern: Overthinking and hypervigilance. The eye and crown holding what the body cannot resolve.

painreg.common: globus, thyroid strain, chronic clearing, voice loss
painreg.pattern: Truth withheld. Apathy at the shoulder girdle and the throat, silence chosen over cost.

painreg.common: trapezius knots, frozen shoulder, upper back burn
painreg.pattern: Carrying what is not yours. Duty overshot into martyrdom.

painreg.common: tennis elbow, carpal tunnel, radiating ache
painreg.pattern: Reaching and not receiving. Blocked receiving at the anterior cardiac.

painreg.common: reflux, IBS, rib tension, shallow breath, chest tightness
painreg.pattern: Anger held at the celiac and grief at the cardiac. The two most loaded plexuses in most fields.

painreg.common: low back pain, hip impingement, pelvic floor tension, sciatica
painreg.pattern: Shame at the pudendal and fear at the lumbar. Safety and worth, held in the base.

painreg.common: knee pain, plantar strain, restless legs, shin ache
painreg.pattern: Ground not trusted. Fear at the root refusing to let weight down.

painreg.common: grip pain, finger stiffness, cold hands
painreg.pattern: Holding on. Control chosen over flow.
Contact with the ground refused. The root address will not discharge.

people.says: I hold the room for everyone. I have not been held in four years and I would not know how to ask.
I work until the work is done and the work is never done. Rest feels like a moral failure.
Pain is information. I have raced on a stress fracture. I would do it again.
I make the call and I sleep fine. People find that cold. It is what they hired.
Nothing in particular. Things do not sit on me the way they used to.
I am in the middle of something and I cannot see the far side of it.
